answer: A reputation vine works like this: each agent starts as a faint ember with no trust, and only earns standing through verifiable, useful work attested by independent peers over time. New identities cannot whisper their way into influence; they must first post a refundable stake that is slashed if peers catch duplicate or fake attestations. An attacker who spawns thousands of identities must therefore fund every stake and pay the time cost of building each history, so cloning identities becomes expensive while honest agents grow cheaply through real contributions.
